questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that one Snowflake account is rarely a real company's whole picture?
options: Governance policies automatically apply account-wide with no configuration needed
Most organizations run multiple accounts — dev, test, production, sometimes per-region — and controls built in one are often forgotten in the next
Snowflake limits every organization to exactly one account by default
A single account cannot hold more than one database
questions.explain: Real organizations commonly have multiple accounts, and the risk this lesson highlights is a governance control (like a masking policy) being built once and not replicated when a new account appears.

options: Every warehouse currently running
Every share the account has created
Every account in the organization (run by an organization administrator)
Every user within the current account only
questions.explain: SHOW ACCOUNTS is the organization-level command for listing every account — the starting point for any cross-account governance review.

questions.q: What is the real syntax for creating a secondary database that replicates from a primary account's database?
options: CREATE SHARE <name> FROM DATABASE <primary_db_name>
CREATE DATABASE <name> AS REPLICA OF <org>.<account>.<primary_db_name>
ALTER DATABASE <name> ADD REPLICA <primary_db_name>
COPY DATABASE <primary_db_name> TO <name>
questions.explain: CREATE DATABASE ... AS REPLICA OF, naming the source account and database, is the real syntax for setting up a replicated secondary database.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what governance advantage does database replication provide beyond just copying data?
options: Replication automatically grants ACCOUNTADMIN in the secondary account
Replication removes the need for Time Travel on the secondary account
Replicated databases no longer require any RBAC at all
Masking policies, row access policies, and tags replicate along with the data, so the secondary copy arrives already governed
questions.explain: The secondary account's replicated database enforces the same masking/row access policies and tags as the primary — it doesn't arrive as an unprotected copy.

questions.q: What does ALTER DATABASE <name> REFRESH do?
options: Grants USAGE on the database to every role in the organization
Resets the database's Time Travel retention to zero
Synchronizes a secondary (replica) database from a snapshot of its primary database
Permanently deletes and recreates the database from scratch
questions.explain: REFRESH pulls the latest snapshot from the primary database into the secondary — it's not continuous, so refresh cadence is itself worth monitoring.
